key_insight: Explicit analytical solutions show that evaporating cylindrical-cap droplets share the same near-contact-line flux and flow power laws as spherical-cap droplets, with flux diverging below 90° contact angles.
engineering_relevance: These solutions provide a simple analytical basis for estimating evaporation-driven contact-line flow in applications such as coating, printing, and droplet deposition.
method: Use conformal mapping to derive evaporative flux for arbitrary contact angles without an arbitrary far-field distance.
Couple the flux to Stokes flow inside the droplet.
Analyze local flow near the liquid–solid–vapour contact line.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical verification of the analytical evaporative-flux expression, but gives no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: The model assumes two-dimensional cylindrical-cap geometry and Stokes flow; matching local power laws does not establish full equivalence to three-dimensional droplets.
paper_title: Some analytical solutions for the evaporative flux and the flow inside a sessile droplet in cylindrical-cap geometry
